title: Stone Game
summary: Alice and Bob play a game with an even number of stone piles in a row.
statement: Alice and Bob play a game with an even number of stone piles in a row. Each pile has a positive number of stones. Alice starts. Players take turns taking all stones from either the start or end of the row. The player with the most stones at the end wins. If both play optimally, determine if Alice wins.
constraints: piles has even length and odd total; players optimally take one end each turn.
Return whether the first player wins.
hints: For an interval, track current player’s maximum score advantage over the opponent.
Choose left or right and subtract the opponent’s optimal remaining advantage.
Zero-sum optimal play makes positive final advantage exactly equivalent to a first-player win.
editorial: Zero-sum optimal play makes positive final advantage exactly equivalent to a first-player win.

tests.explanation: Optimal play lets the first player secure more stones.
The first player can choose a parity strategy and win.
